# fhirpg

> Import HL7 FHIR data into a PostgreSQL database and work with it relationally:
> one table per resource type, resource bodies as `jsonb`, plus history tables
> and stored procedures for create, read, update, and delete. A Rust translation
> of fhirbase.

fhirpg is a command-line tool, not a library. It requires PostgreSQL 18 or
newer and defaults to FHIR R5 (5.0.0), while supporting every version back to
1.0.2.

## Commands

- `fhirpg init` — create the schema: a table and a history table per resource
  type, the `transaction` sequence, and the stored procedures.
- `fhirpg load <paths…|url>` — load resources from NDJSON, FHIR Bundles, or
  single-resource JSON files, gzipped or not, detected by content rather than
  filename. A Bulk Data URL is downloaded first, then loaded.
- `fhirpg transform <file>` — apply the storage transformation to one resource
  and print the result. Useful for understanding what gets stored.
- `fhirpg bulkget <url> <dir>` — run a Bulk Data export and save the NDJSON.
- `fhirpg web` — a browser SQL console, bound to localhost.

Connection flags are libpq's, and honour `PGHOST`, `PGPORT`, `PGUSER`,
`PGDATABASE`, `PGPASSWORD`, `PGSSLMODE`.

## The storage transformation

Resources are rewritten before storage, and queries must account for it:

- Choice elements collapse, with the type moved inside:
  `{"deceasedBoolean": true}` becomes `{"deceased": {"boolean": true}}`.
- References split into id and type: `{"reference": "Patient/1"}` becomes
  `{"resourceType": "Patient", "id": "1"}`. This makes SQL joins possible
  without string parsing.
- The reference rewrite is lossy: `identifier`, `type` and extensions on a
  `Reference` are discarded. This is deliberate, inherited from fhirbase.
- The transformation is not idempotent. Never re-transform a resource read back
  out of the database.

## Load modes

`insert` batches `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`; `copy` streams
`COPY … FROM STDIN`. `insert` is the default for local files, `copy` for Bulk
Data URLs. A `COPY` targets one table, so `copy` is fastest when resources of
the same type are adjacent and very slow when they interleave — measured at 1.2s
grouped against 43.2s non-grouped for the same 127,454 resources. `copy` cannot
skip duplicate ids; `insert` keeps the first occurrence.

- [README](README.md): purpose, install, quick start, performance.
- [The book](book/src/SUMMARY.md): getting started, the storage model, loading,

- [doc/r5-generation/validation.md](doc/r5-generation/validation.md): how the
  generated FHIR R5 assets were validated against fhirbase's own.

## Notes for answering questions about this project

- The stored procedures are `fhirpg_*`, not `fhirbase_*`; the two tools cannot
  operate on each other's databases.
- The `web` command executes arbitrary SQL with no authentication. It binds
  127.0.0.1 by default and warns loudly when bound elsewhere.
- There is no telemetry, no self-update, and no third-party tracking in the web
  console — all three are present in fhirbase and were removed deliberately.
- `--validate` needs a build with the `validate` feature and applies to R5. It
  reports non-conformance; it never rejects data.
